newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil launches privatization of sanitation sector.
newsitem.headline: Brazil launches privatization of sanitation sector.

text.p: Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) has announced the winning consortium which will draw up a model for the privatization of the country's sanitation sector.

BNDES Director Fernando Perrone said a consortium led by Brazilian bank Banco Graphus which also included Engevix Engenharia, Union Bank of Switzerland, Arthur Andersen and local law firm Branco Advogados Associados had won the bid to design the privatization model.

"In 100 days we will have a model that will stimulate private investment in the sanitation sector," Perrone said. "There will be privatizations as well as partnerships between the public and private sectors."

He said the sanitation sector needed investments of $2.5 billion a year over the next 15 years in order to ensure water and sewage services to the whole of Brazil's urban population, but the sector was currently only investing roughly $1 billion.
"We hope private industry will contribute a substantial part of these investments," Perrone said. "There is much inefficiency and investment levels are low."

He said the BNDES and federal mortgage bank Caixa Economica Federal (CEF) would create a $30 million credit line to help municipalities prepare for the privatization of sanitation services. The Inter-American Development Bank (IADB) is also expected to offer further loans worth another $30 million, Perrone added.

Brazil has 5,700 municipalities of which 1,300 are directly responsible for water and sewage services, while the vast remainder grant concessions to Brazil's 27 state-owned companies to provide the services for them.
The 27 state-owned sanitation firms alone posted a turnover of 5.1 billion reais ($4.72 billion) in 1995.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 507 4151))
